To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the development of informal networking between personnel of different agencies, based on horizontal contacts and trust, is crucial for effective cooperation in counterterrorism and crime; (2) this informal networking is a bottom-up, grassroots phenomenon; (3) it is a process that is not limited to the national level, but can be observed on the local, national and international levels; (4) it is a dynamic process that is constantly evolving, and that can be observed on all three levels.

informal networks of law enforcement officers are formed in the process of addressing terrorism and trans-national crime, and these networks are based on horizontal contacts between personnel from different agencies, interpersonal trust and professional identity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of informal inter-agency networks that are built around horizontal contacts, interpersonal and professional trust and common professional values and identity.
how the network approach to counterterrorism and crime can be applied in practice, and how it can be scaled up from a local to a national or international level.
the informal, interpersonal networks that are emerging in the context of globalisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
informal networking is a key element of the success in countering terrorism.
the development of horizontal networks is a necessary, but not sufficient condition for effective counter-terrorism and crime control.
there is no one best approach to countering terrorism and transnational organised crime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to be successful, inter-agency networking should not be based only on formal liaison channels, but also should include informal networks based on interpersonal trust.
, in order to be successful, informal networks need to be built on the foundation of formal structures.
informal networking is a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for the success of inter-agency cooperation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of informal horizontal networks is an essential element of the success of any counter terrorism and transnational organized crime efforts.
informal networks can be used to develop a more comprehensive approach to countering terrorism and transnational organized crime.
informal networks based on interpersonal trust and common identity are a critical factor in countering transnational threats.
